title: Street Food Around the World
description: Why street food is popular, what it tells us about culture, and how to enjoy it safely.
instructions: Read the article about street food, then choose the best answer for each question.

paragraphs.text: In almost every country, you can find people cooking and selling food on the street. Street food is usually cheap, quick and full of flavour, which makes it popular with workers, students and tourists. It is often sold from small carts, stalls or vans that can move from place to place. For many travellers, trying local street food is one of the best ways to discover a new culture.

Each region has its own famous dishes. In Mexico, tacos filled with meat, beans or vegetables are sold on busy corners. In Vietnam, people sit on low plastic stools to eat bowls of hot noodle soup for breakfast. In Turkey, sellers grill meat and wrap it in thin bread, while in India, crispy snacks are served with spicy sauces.

Street food is also important for local economies. Running a food stall requires much less money than opening a restaurant, so it gives many people a chance to start their own business. Recipes are often passed down from parents to children, and some families have sold the same dish in the same spot for generations. In this way, street food helps to keep traditional cooking alive.

However, some visitors worry about hygiene when eating outdoors. A useful tip is to choose stalls with long queues of local customers, because popular stalls usually serve fresh food. It is also wise to watch the food being cooked and to make sure it is served hot. With a little care, street food can be a safe and memorable part of any trip.

In recent years, street food has also become fashionable in places where it was once rare. In many European and North American cities, food trucks park outside offices at lunchtime, offering everything from Korean barbecue to fresh pizza. Old warehouses and car parks are turned into weekend markets where dozens of sellers cook side by side. Some young chefs prefer to start with a food truck rather than a restaurant, because it lets them test their ideas cheaply and move to wherever the customers are.

Life as a street food seller, however, is not always easy. Sellers often work very long hours, starting early to buy fresh ingredients and finishing late at night. They have to cope with heat, rain and cold, and their income can change a lot from day to day. In some cities, the authorities have moved stalls away from busy streets to reduce traffic or improve cleanliness. Supporters of the sellers argue that such rules can destroy small businesses and take away part of the city's character.

Perhaps the greatest charm of street food is the way it brings people together. At night markets in many Asian cities, families, friends and strangers share tables and try each other's dishes. Office workers and students stand side by side at the same counter. Unlike a formal restaurant, there are no reservations and no dress code. Whether it is a simple snack or a full meal, street food offers a taste of everyday life, and that is something no guidebook can fully describe.

questions.text: What is the best title for this passage?
options: How to Open a Restaurant
The Dangers of Eating Outdoors
Breakfast in Vietnam
Street Food: Cheap, Tasty and Full of Culture

evidence.quote: Street food is usually cheap, quick and full of flavour
trying local street food is one of the best ways to discover a new culture
